rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Here is a pattern we keep seeing. A small non-profit does excellent work.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Funders notice, and crowd in. The organisation hires, and grows. And once it is large, it gets worse at the work that made it worth funding.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: What if you could stay small, and still reach more people?

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: That is the whole premise of this film. This is the era of the underdog.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Take one job we know well, coaching a teacher. A coach travels to the school, watches a lesson, and talks it through. About forty dollars a visit.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Now the same coaching, rebuilt. The teacher records the lesson on a phone.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: The recording goes to an AI model, the kind of software behind a chat assistant. It scores the lesson against the scoring guide the government already uses.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: A voice note comes back, in the teacher's language.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Around seventy cents. Across some six thousand sessions, its scores matched human scorers about four times in five. The coach now goes where a person is needed most.

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Every organisation pays in two ways. What it builds once is called a fixed cost.
rows.name: a fixed cost
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: What it repeats for every person it serves is a variable cost.
rows.name: a variable cost
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Prologue
rows.text: Work like that is built and kept running by a workforce you never see. To meet it, try a thought experiment.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: Tomorrow morning, three hundred very talented strangers arrive at your organisation, wanting to help.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: They can do almost anything. They know nothing about you. And when a task ends, they forget what they learned.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: Leave them to it, and this is day one.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: Two start the same job. One is buried in instructions. One puts untested work live.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: A queue forms at one person's desk. And downstairs, nobody hears what a meeting decided.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: The strangers are not people. Each one is an AI agent.
rows.name: an AI agent
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: An agent is an AI model with tools. It uses them, step by step, to finish a task.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: Three hundred is a thought experiment. Start with three, and the problems are the same.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: So what would you build, so that all of them can help? The same things a good organisation builds for any new colleague. It comes down to five questions.

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: People work above the surface. Agents work below it. We call this a shadow organisation.
rows.name: a shadow organisation
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: The three hundred
rows.text: Ours runs at Taleemabad, an education organisation in Pakistan. Teachers and the team know it by one name, Rumi.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: First question. Do they know who is doing what, what our rules are, and what is off limits?

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Two strangers start the same job. A third has nothing to do. Nobody can see it.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: So every job becomes a card on one shared board. Each card is called a bead.
rows.name: a bead
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 168 (iv): card 0.3 s before the name's first word, never before the previous sentence ends (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Before an agent starts, it puts its name on the card.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: If two reach for the same card, the first name sticks. The second takes the next job.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Every card keeps who took the job, and how long it took. Nearly fourteen thousand so far.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Our newcomer has a job, and no idea how we do it.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: And it can only hold so much at once, like a desk. When the desk is full, things fall off. That desk is called a context window.
rows.name: a context window
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: So we write down how we work, one kind of job at a time. Each is a folder of plain instructions, called a skill.
rows.name: a skill
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 168 (iv): card 0.3 s before the name's first word, never before the previous sentence ends (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Every agent starts with a short list, one line per skill. The skill itself opens only when a job needs it.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Some skills are enormous. Our lesson-plan skill holds more than four thousand files.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: So its first page is a map, and says when to go deeper.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: A short summary first, and more depth only when the job calls for it. Remember this shape.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Skills are advice, and advice gets skipped. Some things must never happen unchecked.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: Putting untested work live. Telling a whole region about an outage. Letting internal details slip into a message.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: So before an action like that, a small piece of code runs, and it can refuse. Each of these is called a hook.
rows.name: a hook
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 168 (iv): card 0.3 s before the name's first word, never before the previous sentence ends (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: We have fifty-four, most written after something went wrong.

rows.chapter: Stage 1 · Do they know our rules, who is doing what, and what is off limits?
rows.text: One of them guards the board. No card, no work.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: Second question. Where do we talk to them?

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: They come to where the team already works. Quick questions go in the team chat, which for us is Slack.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: Tag Rumi, and the answer comes back in the thread.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: Deep work needs more room. The agent says where things stand. The product manager says, let me know when you're done.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: Later, a link arrives. It opens a page in Notion, with the mockups and the open questions.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: They settle it there, in comments.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: Finished work lands in the documents and email the team uses.

rows.chapter: Stage 2 · Where do we talk to them?
rows.text: The team sees one colleague. Below the surface, it is as many agents as the job needs.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: Third question. How do they find out what is going on? Much of what an organisation knows is said out loud, and never written down.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: Upstairs, a team changes how it writes lesson plans. Downstairs, nobody hears.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: So we built a meeting note taker of our own. It joins a call when someone invites it.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: About thirteen hundred meetings so far, each one kept where any agent can find it.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: Here is that shape again. A short summary first, and more depth only when needed. It is called progressive disclosure.
rows.name: progressive disclosure
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: Each meeting is stored in layers. On top, one line. Under it, a summary. At the bottom, every word.

rows.chapter: Stage 3 · How do they find out what is going on?
rows.text: Ask what that team decided, and an agent reads the top lines, opens one summary, and answers. It does not need the transcript.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Fourth question. Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Here is where skills come from. A person does the job once, and talks it through. An agent writes the steps down as a skill.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Work it out once, and use it every time after. That is a fixed cost, paid once, shared by every later job.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: A correction can become a new line in the skill. Our lesson-plan skill carries a hundred and fifty-five. This is where a general AI starts to sound like you.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Three hundred agents produce more than anyone can read. But you have already written down what good looks like, in the skill.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: So a second AI model marks the work against it. A check like this is called an eval.
rows.name: an eval
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: The second model gets the work and the standard, and nothing else. It is called a blind judge.
rows.name: a blind judge
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Beside every score it writes its reason, and quotes the line.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: Before we trust a judge, we test it against people's marks. Then its bar is enforced. Work under it goes back to be revised.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: In one region, about nineteen lesson plans in twenty cleared it.

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: The board, the skills, the hooks, the judges. All of it sits around the AI model, and it has a name. The harness.
rows.name: the harness
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 4 · Does the work sound like us, and is it good enough?
rows.text: The model is rented. The harness is yours. In our experience, the stronger the harness, the cheaper the model that can do the job.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Fifth question. What happens when the volume grows? Agents get stuck, and jobs loop.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Someone has to know where to look. That person is called an operator.
rows.name: an operator
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Our advice is to have one from the start.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: One agent alone on a big job is slow, and nobody argues with it.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: So big jobs go to a team. One member's only job is to find faults. That is an agent team.
rows.name: an agent team
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: This film was made by an agent team. Its fault-finders sent this script back more than once.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Three hundred agents should not run all day. When someone tags Rumi, the chat sends a notice, called a webhook.
rows.name: a webhook
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: It reaches a small service that never sleeps, and that wakes one agent. A hook stops. A webhook wakes.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Notice one thing about every agent you have met so far. Each one waits to be asked. That kind of agent is reactive.
rows.name: reactive
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: Our meeting note taker no longer waits. Before each team meeting, it reads past meetings, the team chat, our Notion pages and our product data.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: It reads only the meetings marked public. It writes a short brief, and every point names its source. So it walks in knowing what other teams have just done.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: In the meeting, when it has a point worth making, it raises its hand, unasked. Its point appears in writing, and it speaks when invited. That is running today.

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: An agent that acts before anyone asks is called proactive.
rows.name: proactive
rows.name_card_rule: ruling 163 (b) / lead 044931 (b): card on the name first word (fast film only)

rows.chapter: Stage 5 · What happens when the volume grows?
rows.text: From reactive to proactive. A workforce that spots a gap, and tells you. For us, that move has begun.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: Watch the whole system run once more, for a lender to small farmers. This is how it could work.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: A farmer asks for a tractor, by voice note. A webhook wakes one agent.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: It claims a bead, and opens the lending skill at the step it needs.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: It reads the field photo and the repayment record, and drafts terms.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: A hook stops it approving the loan. That takes a person.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: A blind judge checks the draft. The officer reads one page, and decides.

rows.chapter: The second run
rows.text: The systems you build for agents look a lot like the ones you build for people.

rows.chapter: Sectors, costs and the end
rows.text: The same five questions fit a mental-health helpline, a TB screening team, or a legal-aid service. Those are ideas for now. Ours is running.

rows.chapter: Sectors, costs and the end
rows.text: And those two costs? What you build once gets cheaper, because agents, guided by skills, do much of the building. What you repeat gets cheaper, because agents do the repeating.

rows.chapter: Sectors, costs and the end
rows.text: Growing used to mean hiring, so large organisations won. When reach stops depending on headcount, the advantage moves to the small one.

rows.chapter: Sectors, costs and the end
rows.text: Stay small, stay lean, and reach more people. It's the era of the underdog.

rows.chapter: Sectors, costs and the end
rows.text: We at our partner are exploring a bootcamp for small organisations that want to build this. If that is you, write to Nadir. The address is on screen.
